problem_statement: The IP address parser can overflow an internal buffer when parsing an address string that includes a port number. This occurs when the provided string length is larger than the actual content, or when the port string is overly long (more than 5 characters). The parser should safely handle these cases by bounding the port string copy to a fixed-size buffer and rejecting port strings that exceed the maximum valid length.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/utils -s tests/net/utils/net.util.asan -s net.util.asan -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The original statement covers the length overflow cases but omits observable behaviours required by the hidden tests: accepting valid short ports when str_len is oversized, and the exact port range/length boundary behaviour. These can be added without dictating an implementation.

problems.detail: The statement says the parser must safely handle oversized supplied lengths, but it is ambiguous whether a valid short port with an oversized length should be accepted or rejected; the hidden tests require it to be accepted.
The hidden tests require that the parser treat the NUL-terminated content as the end when str_len is larger than the actual string, and not read/copy past it.

The hidden tests check exact port-value boundaries (0 and 65535 accepted, 65536 rejected) and the 5/6 character leading-zero boundary (00080 accepted, 000080 rejected), which the statement does not specify.

leak_check.leak_detail: The phrase "by bounding the port string copy to a fixed-size buffer" hints at an internal implementation approach, but the rest of the statement describes public behavior and required outputs. It is not a major leak because it does not name internal helpers, source files, or give exact code.
leak_check.suggested_statement:
The IP address parser can overflow an internal buffer when parsing an address string that includes a port number. This occurs when the provided string length is larger than the actual content, or when the port string is overly long (more than 5 characters). The parser must not overflow in these cases and must reject port components longer than the maximum valid length.

The affected public parser is `net_ipaddr_parse`. When the supplied length is larger than the NUL-terminated content, the parser must respect the NUL-terminated content as the end of the input, so a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address with a valid port in a larger buffer must succeed and produce the correct port. A port component is limited to at most 5 characters; any port component of 6 or more characters must be rejected, even if its numeric value would fit or if it contains leading zeros. The port value must be the numeric value of the port string and must fit in the 16-bit port range: port 0 and port 65535 must be accepted, while 65536 must be rejected.
